title: Pet Theft Claims Need Verified Court and Police Records
excerpt: No court judgment, police seizure, or named incident appears in supplied material. Honest advocacy needs documented facts before describing stolen pets or raids.
body_html:
No verified raid, arrest, seizure, court judgment, location, date, defendant, quantity, or source URL appears here. A story about cages, poison bait, stun guns, forged certificates, or stolen family dogs would require documented records. Inventing those details would betray families, animals, and readers.

Evidence must lead

Publish only named cases with original police, court, veterinary, or public-health sources. Separate pet theft, illegal transport, uninspected slaughter, and household rabies exposure. Do not claim that commercial dog-meat supply chains caused a specific infection without primary evidence.

Health facts remain clear

Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical care. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. See WHO rabies guidance.

Demand action without invented certainty

Vietnamese families and animal defenders can demand transparent investigations, strong veterinary controls, protection for companion animals, and abolition of the dog-meat trade. Sign the national petition calling for nationwide abolition by 2030. Add your name to a public demand for action and follow campaign updates reaching decision-makers.
